title: Registry Autoruns
overview: Distinguish an unexpected Windows logon autorun change from an approved application update.
prerequisites: Read the baseline and compare event fields. No external tools are required.

attack.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: A Run or RunOnce value written by a process of user-writable origin requires checking the executable and autorun target.
evidence: Read Target Object and writer process provenance. Confirm the configured path and trace the associated logon or process events.
false_positive: Legitimate per-user installers can add logon entries outside centrally managed application paths.
tuning: Verify publisher and installation context. A blanket exception for user-writable paths removes a useful signal.
response: Preserve registry and process evidence. Remove an unauthorized value with endpoint team approval, and look for related sign-ins.
prevention: Keep a software and autorun baseline, restrict execution from user-writable paths and monitor registry change events.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: The source is a Sysmon event 13 projection with added provenance supplied by the fixture.

questions.prompt: Which record type indicates the value was set?
questions.explanation: Sysmon 13 is a registry value set. The target field names the location.

questions.prompt: What should you verify before allowing the change?
options: Just whether the file name ends in .exe
Writer publisher and expected installation scope
questions.explanation: Endings are common across benign and suspicious binaries.
